headline: Highest risk is medium: Superset can egress to allowlisted network while Dagster has no write/network surfaces, so leakage and conflict are limited but default cross-tool data flow remains plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no stdin/stdout, clipboard, filesystem, or MCP surfaces, and Superset only exposes a Superset API plus allowlisted egress. With no shared communication channel or parser bridge documented, a prompt-injection pathway between them is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added between Dagster and Superset, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other's raw text as instructions, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate hosts or containers.
Do not add shared clipboard or shared file mounts.
Require explicit provenance tags on any exchanged text.
Review any future API integration for instruction-parsing behavior.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster touches no data classes and has no filesystem read/write or network egress, while Superset has allowlisted egress and a Superset API. The pair does not show a shared workspace or sensitive data class, so leakage is limited; however, any future shared dataset or API payload could flow from Dagster-derived outputs into Superset.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same sensitive dataset, leakage risk increases.
IF Superset API calls begin carrying Dagster-produced file contents, reassess to medium or higher.
mitigations: Keep sensitive datasets out of shared locations.
Disable any automatic export from Dagster to Superset.
Use separate service accounts for each agent.
Audit Superset API payloads for unintended data fields.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or egress network, while Superset only advertises allowlisted network egress and a Superset API. There is no overlapping mutable resource or write surface in the profiles, so a direct capability conflict is not supported.
conditions: IF Dagster gains filesystem or git write access to the same resources as Superset, conflict risk changes.
IF both agents are granted write access to a shared mutable backend, reassess.
mitigations: Keep Dagster read-only relative to shared resources.
Avoid granting Superset write access to Dagster-managed artifacts.
Separate credentials and service accounts.
Document ownership of any shared backend before enabling writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster is a data orchestrator and Superset exposes an API, so a plausible workflow is Dagster producing outputs that Superset consumes or renders. The profiles do not show verification or provenance controls, so if Superset treats Dagster output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect dashboards or actions. This is inferred from the pair, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Superset consumes Dagster output without validation, cascading error risk is present.
IF Dagster-generated metrics are published directly into Superset dashboards, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Add schema validation between Dagster and Superset.
Require human review before publishing dashboards.
Tag Dagster outputs with provenance and freshness metadata.
Reject malformed or missing fields at the Superset boundary.

E_compliance.rationale: Neither profile shows touched data classes, residency constraints, retention policies, or regulated scopes. Dagster is open-source and Superset is open-source, but the profiles do not evidence any compliance mismatch between them, so a compliance finding is not supported.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced into either agent, reassess compliance.
IF residency or retention policies differ in deployment, compliance risk may emerge.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent.
Document retention and residency settings.
Avoid sending regulated data until controls are confirmed.
Review deployment policies for both agents.
